title: US Fed Meeting LIVE: Expectations, time, where to watch Kevin Warsh's speech? How rate decision may impact gold, markets | Stock Market News
text:
US Fed Meeting LIVE: The US Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, October 28, as policymakers assess persistent inflationary pressures, rising oil prices and the approaching US midterm elections. The anticipated pause comes after the central bank raised interest rates in September for the first time in more than three years. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously approved a 25-basis-point increase at its previous meeting, bringing the target interest rate range to 3.75%-4.00%.

The Fed's policy announcement will be followed by interest rate decisions from the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan later this week, keeping global markets focused on the direction of monetary policy.

The Federal Reserve's two-day meeting commenced on October 27, 2026, and is scheduled to end on October 28. The 12-member committee will announce its interest rate decision at 11:30 PM IST (2:00 PM ET).

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is expected to address the media shortly after the announcement. His press conference is scheduled to begin at approximately 12:00 AM IST (2:30 PM ET), giving Indian viewers an opportunity to follow the central bank's assessment of the economy and its policy outlook.

After maintaining an extended pause, the US central bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points in September 2026. This was its first rate increase since 2023 and the first under Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

Despite persistent inflation, supported by elevated energy and grocery prices, markets anticipate that policymakers will keep borrowing costs unchanged at Wednesday's meeting. The approaching US midterm elections, which are just six days away, have also contributed to expectations of a pause, as central banks generally avoid significant policy changes immediately before an election.

However, the prospect of another rate increase has not disappeared. Economists believe the Fed could tighten monetary policy again in December if economic indicators continue to show stronger-than-expected conditions.

According to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in an 83% probability of a US interest rate hike in December. For this week's meeting, futures markets indicate a nearly 90% probability that the Fed will maintain its existing federal funds rate range of 3.75%-4.00%.

Meanwhile, September's inflation figures came in higher than expected, adding to the challenges facing the Federal Reserve as it considers its next policy move.

The market is likely to remain cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy decision, with investors closely tracking the inflation outlook and signals on the future trajectory of interest rates. The expectation is that the Fed will keep rates unchanged in October, but the key focus will be on its commentary and the possibility of further tightening in December. Persistent inflation and elevated energy prices could limit the scope for monetary easing.

China and Hong Kong stocks rebounded on Wednesday, snapping a two-session losing streak as artificial intelligence (AI)-related shares tracked a broader rally across Asian markets. The gains came ahead of the US Federal Reserve's policy decision, with investors monitoring the central bank's outlook for interest rates. Optimism also received a boost from upbeat earnings reported by South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix, lifting sentiment towards semiconductor and AI-linked stocks.

At the close, China's benchmark CSI300 Index and the Shanghai Composite Index gained 0.9% each. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index rose 0.2%, while the technology-heavy Hang Seng Tech Index advanced 1.4%.

Despite recent weakness, gold could be approaching an accumulation zone, according to Renisha Chainani of Augmont. Over the medium term, spanning the next two to three months, prices are expected to establish a base between $3,950 and $4,000. Chainani views this range as strong support and anticipates a potential rebound of 10-15% over the coming weeks. However, gold must sustain above $4,100 for its broader uptrend to resume. Traders will need to watch these technical levels closely while assessing the impact of monetary policy on bullion.

Gold prices have slipped below the crucial $4,000 per ounce mark, opening the possibility of a further decline towards $3,950, or approximately ₹1,40,000. Renisha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont, identified the breach as an important development for bullion traders. The metal's near-term direction will depend on how prices behave around this lower threshold. Investors are also monitoring the US Federal Reserve's policy announcement and upcoming inflation data for signals that could influence gold's next move.

The US Treasury market faces an uncertain outlook despite expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates unchanged this week. Persistent inflation, rising government borrowing and concerns about artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments are weighing on investor sentiment.

According to Reuters, US government bonds have recovered recently after a sharp sell-off pushed yields higher for nearly two months from August. The rebound has come amid concerns about financing challenges in parts of the AI infrastructure sector, raising questions about the sustainability of the investment boom that has become an important driver of the US economy.

The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield has risen 84 basis points in 2026, putting it on track for its biggest annual increase since 2022. Meanwhile, yields on 30-year Treasuries have climbed nearly 50 basis points this year, marking their largest annual increase since 2024.
